tasks.q: 1 вересня, десять сорок п'ять. Дядько Вернон висадив Гаррі на вокзалі й поїхав, сміючись. У квитку написано: платформа дев'ять і три чверті. Але між дев'ятою і десятою — лише цегляна стіна. Ти теж шукаєш цю платформу — і тут з'являються Візлі.
tasks.q_pl: 1 września, za kwadrans jedenasta. Wujek Vernon wysadził Harry'ego na dworcu i odjechał, śmiejąc się. Na bilecie jest napisane: peron dziewięć i trzy czwarte. Ale między dziewiątym a dziesiątym jest tylko ceglana ściana. Ty też szukasz tego peronu — i wtedy pojawiają się Weasleyowie.
tasks.q_en: 1 September, a quarter to eleven. Uncle Vernon has dropped Harry off at the station and driven away laughing. The ticket says Platform Nine and Three-Quarters. But between platforms nine and ten there's only a brick wall. You're looking for the platform too, and then the Weasleys appear.

tasks.label: ПРАВИЛО
tasks.q: Future forms: will = decisions now, predictions, promises (I'll help you with your trunk). be going to = plans already made, predictions from evidence (I'm going to sit by the window. Look, it's going to leave!). Present Continuous = fixed arrangements (We're meeting Ron on the train). Present Simple = timetables (The train leaves at eleven). be about to = very soon.

items.q: At twenty to eleven I was standing between ____ nine and ten, and I didn't understand a thing.
Harry was standing nearby. His uncle had just ____ him off and left.
The guard said that platform didn't ____.
Suddenly we heard: “____ with Muggles, of course!”
It was a red-haired family with an owl: the Weasleys.
Mrs Weasley said: “Just walk ____ at the barrier.”
“Best to ____ at it if you're nervous.”
Harry closed his eyes and ran. I was sure he was going to crash into the ____.
But he simply vanished! Then I ran too.
On the other side stood a red ____: the Hogwarts Express.
A red-haired boy, Ron, was sitting there. “Anyone sitting there? Everywhere else is ____.”
At exactly eleven the train ____, and Mrs Weasley waved to us.
I thought: “This journey is going to change everything.” And I was right.
